# Testing and Quality Gates

Status: Draft v1 (lite, 2026-09-30)

Reviewed: 2026-09-30 · consistency review 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-04

This document says how DripNepal is tested and which checks stop a change from merging or a release from shipping. It owns the test strategy, the test layers and tooling, the mandatory test sets, the CI quality gates and the test ID registry. It is sized for a team of one or two developers [Confirmed, Q1]: every check either protects money, stock, tenancy or personal data, or is cheap enough to run on every pull request. It points to the documents that own the behaviour under test instead of restating it.

Related documents: [00 Context](00-context-assumptions-and-questions.md) · [01 Requirements](01-product-requirements.md) · [02 Journeys](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md) · [03 Architecture](03-system-architecture.md) · [04 Domain model](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md) · [04a Tables](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md) · [05 Lifecycles](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md) · [06 API](06-api-design.md) · [07 Security](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md) · [08 UI](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md) · [09 Code standards](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md) · [11 Operations](11-deployment-and-operations.md) · [12 Roadmap](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md) · [Risks and open decisions](risks-and-open-decisions.md) · [ADRs](adr/README.md)

Labels follow [00 §1.2](00-context-assumptions-and-questions.md#12-evidence-labels). A package that is not in `package.json` today is marked proposed. Code blocks are pseudocode.

## 1. Scope and how to read this document

This lite version is enough to build the harness in M0 and give every test a stable ID; [§8](#8-expanding-this-document) lists what the full version adds.

The behaviour a test asserts belongs to the document named in its registry row: lifecycles to [05](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md), the API to [06](06-api-design.md), permissions to [07](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md), UI to [08](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md). Folder layout, lint and hooks belong to [09](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md); the pipeline, staging and drills to [11](11-deployment-and-operations.md); milestones and requirement-to-test traceability to [12](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md).

- **The registry (§6) is the single source of test IDs.** Other documents cite IDs; this one defines them. If a document and a row disagree, the owning document wins on behaviour and §6 wins on the number.
- **Base IDs.** Fourteen IDs were fixed before the documents were written and keep their numbers and meaning: `T-SEC-001` to `T-SEC-004`, `T-SEC-010`, `T-INV-003`, `T-PAY-005`, `T-PAY-008`, `T-CHK-004`, `T-ARCH-001`, `T-API-001`, `T-A11Y-001`, `T-PERF-001`, `T-OPS-001`. Other documents label them "base (10 §6)".
- **Everything else is registered here**, including IDs other documents marked "(proposed)". Registered does not mean written (§6.1).
- **Area references** such as "T-CAT area" in [01](01-product-requirements.md) and [02](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md) stay valid; the test gets its number under §6.1 when it is written.

## 2. Test strategy

Risk-first: name how the marketplace can fail its users, and give each failure a layer that can see it.

### 2.1 Top risks and where they are caught

| Risk                                                      | Layer that catches it                                                     | Test IDs                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cross-shop data leakage (INV-02)                          | Functional tests generated from the route list; composite-FK insert tests | `T-SEC-001`, `T-SEC-005`, `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-036`, `T-ORD-104`, `T-MED-101`                |
| Money errors (INV-06, INV-10, INV-11)                     | Unit property tests; a golden functional test; CHECK tests                | `T-LED-001`, `T-ORD-008`, `T-ORD-106`, `T-ARCH-013`, `T-SEC-004`, `T-ORD-102`, `T-LED-104`  |
| Oversell (INV-04, INV-05)                                 | Concurrency suite on real PostgreSQL                                      | `T-INV-003`, `T-INV-001`, `T-CHK-009`, `T-INV-004`                                          |
| Duplicate orders (INV-22)                                 | Concurrency suite; one browser test of a dropped response                 | `T-CHK-004`, `T-CHK-005`, `T-API-007`, `T-UI-017`                                           |
| Payment spoofing or a missed capture (R1.1)               | Functional tests with the scripted fake provider; concurrency suite       | `T-PAY-001` to `T-PAY-005`, `T-PAY-010`, `T-SEC-021`, `T-PAY-008`                           |
| Suspended or stolen sessions keep working                 | Functional tests that drive the session store and the revocation job      | `T-SEC-010`, `T-SEC-009`, `T-SEC-011`, `T-IAM-109`                                          |
| Retention or anonymisation removes too much or too little | Functional tests through the real actions; two-role tests                 | `T-IAM-106`, `T-IAM-111`, `T-IAM-112`, `T-SEC-102`, `T-ARCH-012`, `T-SHOP-004`, `T-ADM-011` |
| Data loss (bad migration, lost backup)                    | CI schema checks; release checks; restore drills                          | `T-ARCH-010`, `T-ARCH-017`, `T-OPS-013`, `T-OPS-014`, `T-OPS-001`                           |

Every invariant of [04 §16.2](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#162-invariant-register) names at least one ID in §6.

### 2.2 No coverage percentage; mandatory sets instead

There is no line-coverage target. Coverage shows which lines ran, not whether two checkouts raced or shop B's ID was tried on shop A's route: a sequential `placeOrder` test reaches full coverage with the lock removed. Coverage may be printed but never gates. Instead:

1. The **mandatory sets** of §4 are green on every pull request; most are generated from the route list, the permission maps or the schema catalogue.
2. **A rule changes with its test.** A pull request that changes a rule in [04a](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md), [05](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md), [06](06-api-design.md) or [07](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md) changes or adds the test that rule cites, and names it in the "Tests added or changed" line of the [09 §11.5](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#115-pull-request-template-and-review-checklist) template.
3. **Each acceptance criterion is automated at the lowest reliable layer** ([02 §7](02-user-journeys-and-acceptance-criteria.md#7-journey-completion-checklist)), and the test title cites its AC ID (§6.1).

### 2.3 What not to test heavily

- **Framework internals** (Lucid, VineJS, Inertia, Radix, pg-boss): test DripNepal's configuration, queries and constraints.
- **Copied shadcn components**: covered on the composed page by `T-A11Y-001` and the keyboard pass of [08 §9.4](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#94-how-it-is-verified).
- **Visual snapshots**: none in R1.
- **Serializers one by one**: `T-API-001` validates every response shape.
- **A mocked database**: anything that runs SQL runs on PostgreSQL 18.4, never SQLite (RF-32).
- **Real providers in CI**: never ([11 §2.3](11-deployment-and-operations.md#23-ci)); sandboxes are the manual M8 acceptance (VX-06, VX-07).
- **Business rules through the browser**: asserted through the API; the browser suite covers UI behaviour, accessibility and a few journeys.

### 3.2 The test database

- **Separate database** `dripnepal_test`; boot refuses a `DB_DATABASE` without the `_test` suffix under `NODE_ENV=test` ([09 §6.1](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#61-variable-catalogue), RF-32). `.env.test` sets `DB_DATABASE=dripnepal_test`, the cross-field policy in `start/env.ts` refuses any other name (`T-ARCH-024`), and the development Compose file's init script creates the database ([11 §4.3](11-deployment-and-operations.md#43-development-compose-rf-43-fix-list)) [Verified-repo `.env.test`, `start/env_policy.ts`, `docker/postgres/init/01_create_test_database.sql`]. CI uses the `postgres:18.4` service container and the SeaweedFS container of [11 §2.3](11-deployment-and-operations.md#23-ci).
- **Two roles, as in production.** Migrations run as `dripnepal_migrator`, tests as `dripnepal_app` ([07 §4.10](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#410-database-roles-and-grants)), so the revoked privileges behind `T-ARCH-012` and `T-SEC-029` are real. Migrations use the `pg_migrator` connection that [09 §6.1](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#61-variable-catalogue) defines from `DB_MIGRATOR_*` under `NODE_ENV=test`.
- **Migrations once per run.** The runner setup hook drops every table and runs the migrations, then the reference seeders, on the migrator connection; Lucid's test utilities pass a connection name to Ace as `--connection` [Verified-repo `@adonisjs/lucid` 22.4.2 `build/src/test_utils/database.js:23-26`]. It runs `db:wipe` and then `migration:run --no-schema-generate` rather than `migration:fresh`, because `migration:fresh` does not pass `--no-schema-generate` on to `migration:run` [Verified-repo `@adonisjs/lucid` 22.4.2 `build/commands/migration/fresh.js`, `getMigrateArgs`], and a test run must not rewrite the generated `database/schema.ts` ([09 §1.4](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#14-generated-artefacts)) [Verified-repo `tests/support/database.ts`]. The roles exist before the run: CI creates them in a step before the migrations, and the development Compose init script creates them with the test database, which the migrator owns ([11 §2.3](11-deployment-and-operations.md#23-ci), [11 §4.3](11-deployment-and-operations.md#43-development-compose-rf-43-fix-list)) [Verified-repo `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docker/postgres/init/00_create_roles.sql`].
- **The `pgboss` schema comes from the same hook.** Every pg-boss instance starts with its migration disabled (tech lead decision, 2026-10-01), so no instance creates the schema. After the migrations and before the reference seeders, the hook runs the pg-boss schema step and the idempotent `pgboss` grants to `dripnepal_app` as the migrator, in the order of the release step ([11 §5.4](11-deployment-and-operations.md#54-the-deploy-step-on-a-host), [09 §2.3](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#23-how-modules-cooperate), [09 §6.1](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#61-variable-catalogue) "Test roles", [11 §6.1](11-deployment-and-operations.md#61-where-and-how-migrations-run)). The job-row assertions of §3.6 need it. Since 2026-11-11 the step is `node ace jobs:install` (`T-ARCH-004`). `db:wipe` drops only `public`, so the hook drops schema `pgboss` first, as the migrator: each run starts from a fresh install, with no jobs left from an earlier run.

```ts
// tests/support/database.ts, run setup (as built; the pg-boss step since 2026-11-11)
setup: [
  async () => {
    const ace = await app.container.make('ace')
    await ace.exec('db:wipe', ['--connection=pg_migrator'])
    await ace.exec('migration:run', ['--connection=pg_migrator', '--no-schema-generate'])
    // pg-boss schema install or upgrade, then the idempotent pgboss grants, as the migrator
    // (09 §2.3, 11 §6.1; T-ARCH-004), after dropping the pgboss schema of the last run
    await db.connection('pg_migrator').rawQuery('DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS pgboss CASCADE')
    await ace.exec('jobs:install', ['--connection=pg_migrator'])
    // the reference seeder files of 09 §8.8, passed with --files as the release step does
    await ace.exec('db:seed', ['--connection=pg_migrator', ...referenceSeederFileFlags])
  },
]
```

### 3.3 Isolation, and why concurrency tests are different

**No truncation.** `testUtils.db().truncate()` returns a teardown that runs `db:truncate`, one `TRUNCATE` over every table of the `public` schema [Verified-repo `@adonisjs/lucid` 22.4.2 `build/src/test_utils/database.js:43-46`, `build/commands/db_truncate.js:44`, `build/src/dialects/pg.js:125-144`], which the `BEFORE TRUNCATE` triggers of the append-only tables abort ([04 §2.12](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#212-append-only-tables)). The harness must not need a hole in those triggers.

**Functional and browser suites** wrap each test in `testUtils.db().wrapInGlobalTransaction()`, rolled back afterwards [Verified-repo `build/src/test_utils/database.js:67-71`]; the action's `withTx` transactions become savepoints ([09 §12.10](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#1210-tests)). A test expecting a constraint error runs that statement in a nested transaction so it can continue. Edited 2026-11-26: `tests/bootstrap.ts` wraps only the functional suite so far, because the browser suite has no spec yet. The first browser spec adds the wrap and settles four points found in a read of the sources: (a) Japa's browser plugin closes the browser context after the rollback, so the wrap must close the context first, or a late request from the page commits rows; (b) a real browser's parallel requests share the one transaction, so a plain query of one request runs inside another request's open savepoint and rolls back with it, and a statement that fails outside a savepoint aborts the transaction for the rest of the test; (c) `sessionBrowserClient` writes to the memory session store while tests use the database driver, so a spec signs in through the page or inserts a `sessions` row; (d) limiter rows commit on their own connections, so browser specs delete their keys as below.

**The concurrency suite commits for real, on separate connections.** A global transaction pins the process to one transaction on one PostgreSQL backend: twenty "parallel" checkouts would run one after another, the row lock of [05 §4.5](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#45-the-conditional-stock-update) would never make a second backend wait, and the test would pass with the lock removed. So the suite:

- sends parallel requests over separate pool connections, with `DB_POOL_MAX=20` (the maximum of [09 §6.1](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#61-variable-catalogue)) in the test environment and never more parallel requests than connections, so no request queues for one [Assumption: `placeOrder` holds one connection at a time];
- isolates tests by data, not rollback: each test creates its own shop, users, variants and keys with unique slugs and emails and asserts only on those rows; the next run starts from `migration:fresh`;
- hosts tests that need commits or the second role: triggers and grants (`T-ARCH-012`, `T-SEC-029`), handlers run twice (`T-INV-004`), races (`T-ORD-002`, `T-IAM-107`);
- starts with `T-ARCH-032`: two connections take `FOR UPDATE` on one row and the second must wait, so a harness that stops contending fails first.

**Limiters write outside the test's transaction.** The limiter manager caches each limiter for the life of the process, with the database client it was built on. So the runner's setup builds every limiter of [06 §9.1](06-api-design.md#91-rate-limits) once, before any suite and outside any transaction. Every limiter then writes `rate_limits` on its own pool connection and commits, in every suite, as in production. A test that charges a limiter deletes its keys afterwards. A limiter first built inside a functional test kept that test's global transaction. Its later writes went to whichever transaction next held that connection, in another test or suite. This was found on 2026-11-24 (R1-S part 1c-ii): in the concurrency suite, a wrong code's point rolled back with the action. A limiter built with `limiter.use()` outside `rateLimiter()` would bring the fault back [Verified-repo `tests/bootstrap.ts`].

`configureSuite` starts the HTTP server for `concurrency` too [Verified-repo `tests/bootstrap.ts`].

### 3.4 Factories and reference data

Factories follow [04 §20.3](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#203-seeders-factories-and-schema-generation): they import the vocabularies the CHECK lists mirror, encrypt through the real field-crypto service with a test key and create whole aggregates. Until E6 builds the field-crypto service, they write a placeholder ciphertext instead (04 §20.3, 2026-11-09). `T-ARCH-031` inserts every factory and state into the migrated schema, so a CHECK change the factories miss fails once, in one place. Reference data comes from the reference seeders (§3.2); tests never change it.

### 3.5 Time

Japa's `timeTravel` and `freezeTime` fake the JavaScript `Date` through `timekeeper` [Verified-repo `@japa/runner` 5.3.0 `build/index.js:238-249`], which Luxon reads too. They do not move PostgreSQL's `now()`, which fills `created_at` and `updated_at` ([04 §2.2](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#22-time)) and drives job predicates. So **move data, not clocks** where the database compares with `now()` (an expiry test inserts holds already past `expires_at`); freeze the JavaScript clock only for due times computed in TypeScript; test Kathmandu boundaries at fixed instants such as 18:14:59 and 18:15:00 UTC (`T-UI-020`); never sleep; run jobs by calling their handlers.

### 3.6 Provider fakes, email, storage and jobs

The ports of [03 §11.1](03-system-architecture.md#111-ports) have test doubles chosen by configuration (`PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake`).

- **Scripted `PaymentProvider` fake.** Each test scripts the answers per payment: an `initiate` timeout then a paid `lookup` (timeout-then-success); a failed return while the lookup says `COMPLETE`; a callback after the lookup captured (out of order); an unknown status; a different amount; a refund that times out after the provider processed it (`T-PAY-008`). The fake records calls, so a test can assert "no second refund before a lookup". M8 sandbox payloads become `T-PAY-010` fixtures.

```ts
// pseudocode; the script API is designed with the adapter in M8
fakeProvider.script(payment.id, [
  { call: 'initiate', result: timeout() },
  { call: 'lookup', result: status('COMPLETE', { amount: payment.amount_minor }) },
])
```

- **Email**: a capturing `EmailSender` fake, which keeps each message as the port receives it; tests assert the recipient, the template and the plain-text part, where the values appear, never the HTML. `T-NOT-001` points real SMTP at a closed port instead. Built 2026-11-22 (M1 part 1b): `captureEmails()` in `tests/support/email.ts` binds the fake in the container and returns `{ fake, restore }`; `fake.failNext('retryable' | 'permanent')` makes the next sends fail with `EmailNotSent`, `fake.throwNext(error)` makes the next one throw any other error, and the fake keeps the `PortAdapter` guard, so a send inside a transaction still throws (`T-ARCH-003`).
- **Object storage**: an in-memory fake in the functional and concurrency suites, and SeaweedFS for `T-MED-005`. Edited 2026-11-24 (R1-S part 2d-i, note 89): the functional and concurrency suites bind the in-memory fake of `tests/support/object_storage.ts`, and the S3 adapter is tested over the real SDK and signer, with the client the binding builds, and a canned HTTP handler; `.env.test` blanks `S3_*`. Edited 2026-11-25 (OD-65): `T-MED-005` (`tests/functional/platform/object_storage_s3.spec.ts`) runs the adapter against a real S3 server, the `seaweedfs` service of the development Compose file, which CI's Tests job starts. Edited 2026-11-25 (R1-S part 2d-ii, note 91): the in-memory fake also holds bytes (`upload` with a `Buffer`), and its `read` and `put` behave as the S3 adapter's, `If-Match` and the limit included. Locally `T-MED-005` is skipped while no server answers on `S3_CONTRACT_ENDPOINT` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8333`); CI sets `S3_CONTRACT_REQUIRED=1`, so there a missing server fails it.
- **Jobs**: functional tests assert that the job row was written in the business transaction ([ADR-0010](adr/0010-postgres-jobs-pg-boss-transactional-send.md)); no worker runs during tests.

### 3.7 Contract, accessibility and performance

- **`T-API-001`**: a functional-suite hook validates every `/api/v1` response (status, `Content-Type`, body) against its operation in `docs/openapi.yaml`, OpenAPI 3.1.0 [Verified-repo `docs/openapi.yaml:1`], with schemas compiled once per run in Ajv's JSON Schema 2020-12 mode [Assumption]. `T-API-009` lints the spec and `T-API-010` checks route parity.
- **`T-A11Y-001`**: axe in the browser suite on the core pages of [08 §9.4](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#94-how-it-is-verified), both themes, 360 × 640 and 1280 × 800, each dialog opened once; zero serious or critical violations. Rule tags are WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA [Assumption: tag names and a target-size rule are checked against the axe-core version pinned in M4]. SC 2.5.8 asks for 24 × 24 CSS px targets [Verified-doc [research: ui-frontend](research/ui-frontend.md), <https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>, accessed 2026-09-25]; the 44 px check of 08 is `T-UI-004`.
- **`T-PERF-001`**: k6 against staging at 10× launch load, that is 100 orders in the peak hour, bursts of 10 `placeOrder` a minute and about 20 storefront requests per second ([01 §8](01-product-requirements.md#8-non-functional-requirements), A-02), measured against NFR-PERF-003 (reads p95 ≤ 300 ms) and NFR-PERF-004 (`placeOrder` p95 ≤ 800 ms with contention on popular variants, zero oversells) of [01 §8.2](01-product-requirements.md#82-performance-nfr-perf). Pull requests block on budgets that do not depend on runner speed: `T-PERF-002` (query plans), `T-UI-012` (JavaScript) and `T-UI-031` (page props). `T-PERF-003` (Lighthouse, [08 §10.1](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#101-budgets)) only reports, because shared CI runners make timings noisy.

**`T-PAY-005`, restated.** The base wording was "the same webhook delivered N times (and concurrently) gives one state change and one ledger posting". eSewa ePay and Khalti KPG-2 send no webhooks ([06 §12.1](06-api-design.md#121-what-the-providers-offer), [05 §8.6](05-order-payment-and-inventory-lifecycles.md#86-duplicate-and-out-of-order-provider-events-returns-webhooks-lookups)). The test is: **the same provider event (a return, a lookup result or a callback) delivered N times, sequentially and concurrently, gives one state change, one ledger-relevant event and one email.** The reserved webhook route is one of the delivery paths.

**`T-SEC-010`, expected result**, as [07 §3.3](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#33-the-per-request-account-check-and-the-suspension-decision) decides: with the worker stopped, the suspended user's next API request gets 403 `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` and the next page request redirects to `/login`; after `identity.revoke_sessions` runs, the same cookie gets 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` on a protected `GET` and on a `POST` with the old `X-XSRF-TOKEN`, never a 2xx; a stamp-only mismatch gets 401.

## 5. CI quality gates

[11 §5](11-deployment-and-operations.md#5-cicd-and-release-promotion) owns the pipeline shape (`ci.yml` on pull requests, `release.yml` after merge, staging, a manual production approval) and [09](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md) the tool configuration. This section decides which checks run and which block. Today `ci.yml` runs Prettier, ESLint, both typechecks, the production build, the Docker image build and the unit, functional and concurrency suites on PostgreSQL 18.4, on pushes to and pull requests into `main` [Verified-repo `.github/workflows/ci.yml`]. Edited 2026-11-07: it also runs on pull requests into `feat/e4-schema-baseline`, the E4 integration branch ([12 §4.1](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#41-epics-and-order)), and its Tests job runs `SELECT uuidv7()` and the `T-ARCH-010` step before the suites. Edited 2026-11-09: it can also be started by hand (`workflow_dispatch`), because retargeting a stacked pull request onto the integration branch starts no run. Also edited 2026-11-09: before the migrations the Tests job runs the `T-ARCH-017` lock script in file-name mode and the `T-ARCH-034` extension lint; `T-ARCH-011`, `T-ARCH-013`, `T-ARCH-014` and `T-ARCH-015` run in the suites (note 38). It was added for the single-seller v1 launch, so every other check below is proposed until M0 builds the full `ci.yml`. Built in M0 (E2, 2026-11-15, note 49): `ci.yml` has one job per stage of §5.1 that M0 can run: Static, Repository, Supply chain, Contract, Tests (the Database, Functional and Concurrency stages, on one PostgreSQL service) and Docker image. The job names are the required status checks of §5.4. The Browser stage, the kit and licence checks and the `T-API-001` hook come with E3, E10 and M1 (§5.4). Edited 2026-11-09: on the integration branch the suites no longer hold v1 tests (note 40); the branch's merge into `main` brings that state to `main`.

Decisions in this table:

- **The concurrency and browser suites run in `ci.yml`**, beside those of [11 §5.2](11-deployment-and-operations.md#52-workflows): G1 of [01 §5.3](01-product-requirements.md#53-r1-launch-gates) needs `T-INV-003` and `T-CHK-004` green in CI.
- **The image smoke also runs on pull requests**, not only in `release.yml`, so an SSR break (RF-08) never reaches `main`.
- **`T-ARCH-030` blocks from M0.** It fails on absolute home-directory paths and on the names of local-only planning sources, kept in a denylist next to the script so that `docs/` never spells them. The denylist matches paths and source names, not ordinary words, so the `audit` module of [09 §2.2](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#22-allowed-dependencies) and the word "canonical" pass. The consistency review removes the existing references document by document; if its final cross-document check still finds one when M0 builds `ci.yml`, the check only warns until that reference is gone. Edited 2026-11-15 (E2, note 49): the check reads every tracked text file, not only `docs/`, because [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#keep-the-repository-self-contained) applies the rule to the whole repository; the denylist is `scripts/portability_denylist.txt`. It holds the path patterns; the names of local-only planning sources are added there by the product owner, who knows them. The consistency review's final check found no local reference, so the check blocks.
- **The weekly dependency update** may change `pnpm-lock.yaml` without `package.json`: `T-SEC-026` exempts pull requests labelled `dependencies` [Assumption: the update bot applies it] ([09 §10.2](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#102-lockfile-version-ranges-and-install-behaviour)). Edited 2026-11-15 (E2): the Supply chain job reads the pull request's labels when it runs, so a maintainer who adds the label re-runs the job instead of pushing again.
- **Hooks are convenience**; pre-push runs typecheck and the unit suite ([09 §11.4](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#114-git-hooks-husky-9)).
- **Raw-text lint is deferred to E10** (2026-11-15, note 49; built 2026-11-20, note 57). [09 §11.2](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#112-eslintconfigjs) planned `react/jsx-no-literals` as a warning in M0, but the Static stage runs ESLint on the whole tree with zero warnings, so every existing page would fail CI. The rule is added with the `resources/lang/en` catalogs of E10 ([12 §4.1](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#41-epics-and-order)), per surface as [08 §13](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#13-current-ui-remediation-list) moves it.
- **The secret scan reads the full history on every pull request** (`T-SEC-025`, 2026-11-15). It took about 10 s over the 2,500 text blobs of the local clone. If it grows past about 10 minutes, it moves to a scheduled and manual job, and pull requests scan the tree.

### 5.3 Flaky and quarantined tests

- `.retry()` is not used; a CI step fails on it. A retried race test hides the bug it exists to find.
- A flaky test is fixed within two working days or quarantined with `.skip(true, 'quarantine: <issue link>')` and the `@quarantine` tag. CI lists quarantined tests in the job summary and fails when one is older than 14 days.
- Base IDs and §4 sets are never quarantined; the merge waits for the fix.
- Browser tests wait for conditions, never for fixed times.

### 5.4 The smallest gate before the first feature code (M0)

Before the first M1 feature pull request, `main` is protected and `ci.yml` blocks on:

1. The Static, Repository, Supply chain and Contract stages of §5.1 (without the kit and licence checks until those files exist).
2. The test database guard and two-role setup (§3.2); `T-ARCH-010`, `T-ARCH-011`, `T-ARCH-012`, `T-ARCH-013`, `T-ARCH-014`, `T-ARCH-015`, `T-ARCH-022` and `T-ARCH-034`, and the `T-ARCH-017` script in file-name mode, as the baseline lands ([09 §8.1](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#81-the-m0-re-baseline-adr-0011-od-01), [12 §4.3](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md#43-exit-criteria) item 2); `T-ARCH-031` for the first factories.
3. The functional suite with the `T-API-001` hook and the M0 behaviours: request IDs (`T-API-005`), the error contract (`T-API-012`, `T-SEC-027`), the stamp-mismatch case of `T-SEC-010` and the auth rate limits (`T-SEC-011`).
4. The concurrency suite with `T-ARCH-032`, so M5 adds tests, not infrastructure.
5. The image build with `T-ARCH-002` (RF-08) and `T-OPS-010`, and the browser smoke.
6. `T-ARCH-030`, blocking, in the Repository stage (warning only while the consistency review's final check still finds a local reference, §5.1).

Built in M0 (E2, 2026-11-15, note 49): `ci.yml` blocks on items 1 and 2 and on the M0 parts of items 3 to 6 that exist. Branch protection on `main` (a repository setting, applied by the tech lead; [09 §11.6](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#116-branches-commits-and-merges)) requires these status checks of workflow `ci`, by job name: `Static`, `Repository`, `Supply chain`, `Contract`, `Tests` and `Docker image`. Applied on 2026-11-19 (note 50): the checks must be reported by GitHub Actions on a branch that is up to date with `main`. Still to come: the functional `T-API-001` hook with the first `/api/v1` operation (M1), the browser smoke and `T-ARCH-032` (E3), and `T-ARCH-002` (E10).

## 6. Test ID registry

Every test ID used in the documentation set, grouped by area and sorted by ID.

### 6.1 Naming and numbering rules

- **Format** `T-<AREA>-<NNN>`, three digits. The areas are the 21 of [00 §1.3](00-context-assumptions-and-questions.md#13-id-schemes): `ARCH`, `API`, `SEC`, `IAM`, `SHOP`, `CAT`, `MED`, `INV`, `CART`, `CHK`, `ORD`, `FUL`, `PAY`, `RET`, `LED`, `NOT`, `ADM`, `OPS`, `UI`, `A11Y`, `PERF`.
- **Two blocks.** In the business areas, `001`–`099` hold behaviour, contract and operations tests and `101`–`199` hold tests of one table's rule in [04](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md) or [04a](04a-data-dictionary-tables.md) (constraints, triggers, indexes and the races around them), as the documents already numbered them. `T-ARCH` checks that span the whole schema stay in `001`–`099`.
- **A new ID** takes the next number after the highest in its block and is added here in the pull request that first cites it.
- **Never reuse a number.** A retired ID keeps its row, marked retired, with its successor.
- **A widened scope keeps the ID** (the owning document states the new case); a different behaviour gets a new ID.
- **Test titles start with the ID** and end with the acceptance criteria they prove, so a search finds both:

```ts
// pseudocode
test('T-INV-003 last unit: one order per run, reserved ≤ on_hand [AC-J05-05]', async () => { … })
```

One ID may have several Japa tests; they share the prefix. `T-ARCH-033` fails on a test ID missing from this section and lists registered IDs no test cites yet.

**Notes column:** "base" is one of the 14 base IDs; "new" means first numbered here; "widened (§7)" means an audit added cases; "widened" alone means the owning document added cases later; "was …" records an earlier number; "R1.1" or "R2" names the release of the behaviour when it is not R1.

## 8. Expanding this document

The full version adds, each when its milestone needs it:

- **Generated permission-matrix tables**: the expected status of every route × role × shop status, printed by the `T-SEC-030` and `T-SEC-031` generators and reviewed against [07 §4](07-security-threat-model-and-permissions.md#4-authorization-model-and-permission-matrix) (M2).
- **Load scenarios and budgets**: k6 arrival rates, catalogue size (A-03), thresholds per NFR-PERF target, and how staging results are read (M7).
- **Browser journeys per J-xx**: which journeys beyond `T-UI-030` block a release, with their fixtures (M4 to M7).
- **Traceability**: FR and AC to test IDs lives in [12](12-roadmap-and-backlog.md); this document adds a generated ID-to-file index from `T-ARCH-033`.
- **Named fixtures and seed volumes**: shops in each status, edge-case carts, the 50,000-listing database of `T-SEC-024` and `T-PERF-002`.
- **M8 provider acceptance**: sandbox scripts per VX-06 or VX-07 and their recorded fixtures.
- **CI time budget**: per-job targets, caching, parallel jobs.
- **Release records**: the format of the manual accessibility pass ([08 §9.4](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#94-how-it-is-verified)) and of launch-gate evidence.

29. **v1 tests and CI (2026-11-04).** For the single-seller v1 launch (risks §2.3, 2026-11-03), the `functional` and `concurrency` suites hold tests of the v1 checkout, cart and order code, and `ci.yml` runs them on PostgreSQL 18.4 for pushes to and pull requests into `main` and `v1` (§3.1, §5). Since #142 merged `v1` into `main`, CI had not run on pull requests into `main`. Each v1 test is tagged `@v1`. It cites a registered ID only where it proves that ID's behaviour on the v1 schema: `T-CHK-010`, `T-ORD-105` and `T-SEC-001` in `functional`, and `T-INV-003`, `T-CHK-009` and `T-ORD-002` in `concurrency`. No new ID is registered. M0 replaces the `@v1` tests with the registered tests of §6 as it rebuilds checkout to 05. The v1 harness differs from §3.2 in two ways: the suite setup in `tests/bootstrap.ts` wipes, migrates and seeds once per run on the default connection, because the two test roles and `pg_migrator` do not exist yet; and it runs `migration:run` with `--no-schema-generate`, so a test run never rewrites `database/schema.ts`. Still open: the two roles (§3.2), `@japa/api-client` and HTTP-level tests (§3.1), and the rest of §5.1. 2026-11-09: the v1 store and these `@v1` tests were removed on the E4 integration branch (#166), and the branch's merge removes them from `main` (note 40). The IDs they cited keep their rows; their tests come with the M5 and M6 actions, and the two roles exist since note 37.

73. **Dead-letter redrive (2026-11-23, M1 part 1c).** Built and recorded in the §6 rows: the dead-letter part of `T-NOT-001` (`tests/concurrency/notifications/email_outage.spec.ts`), in the `concurrency` suite because pg-boss and the command's own instance work on their own connections. As 05 §8.14 asks, the group sets the `notifications.send_email` queue to one retry, due at once, and puts the 03 §9 settings back afterwards. The queues are worked as `jobs:work` works them (the registered handler, then pg-boss's complete or fail), and the redrive is the command itself: an outage dead-letters every job and leaves its row `queued`; a preview changes nothing; two batches move the dead letters back; each `queued` row is then sent exactly once, a row made `failed` meanwhile is never sent, a second redrive finds nothing, and the output holds no payload value. A second test leaves a dead letter past its retention in place and fails, without a send, a token email whose token expired while it waited. `T-OPS-025` is new: `jobs:redrive` behaviour ([09 §9.7](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#97-dead-letter-redrive-node-ace-jobsredrive)), the refusals (a name that is not the dead-letter queue of an application queue, `dlq.refunds.execute` among them, a rule mismatch either way, a limit out of range), `--discard` oldest first within `--limit`, its dry run, and no payload in the output (`tests/concurrency/platform/jobs_redrive.spec.ts`). The worker's error classification is unchanged ([09 note 116](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). After the Fable review (2026-11-23): `T-OPS-025` adds a rule for every queue of `JOB_QUEUES`, `--discard --dry-run` on a redriven queue, a non-numeric `--limit` (refused by Ace before the command runs), a dead-letter queue `jobs:install` has not created (removed and put back as the migrator), and a scan that loses its page anchor and starts again; the §6 row now says what it tests. The partial-move exit 1 has no test, because it needs another run to win the race between the read and the move. The `T-NOT-001` spec deletes `T-OPS-025`'s probes in its own clean-up, and its header notes that a killed run leaves `notifications.send_email` at one retry until the next `jobs:install`.

Of fourteen deliberate breaks, thirteen failed a test; the other, the validator's trim of the alt text, changes nothing over HTTP, because the JSON body parser already trims strings (the `@adonisjs/bodyparser` default `trimWhitespaces`) and turns an empty one into null (`convertEmptyStringsToNull` in `config/bodyparser.ts`) ([06 note 71](06-api-design.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).

Of twenty deliberate breaks, nineteen failed a test; the other drops `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM img)` from the visibility rule, which the statement's `CROSS JOIN img` already enforces (an equivalent change). The per-product advisory lock of the listing job has no race test ([04 note 55](04-domain-model-and-data-dictionary.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
94. **The publish lifecycle's tests (2026-11-26, R1-S part 2e-ii).** §6.5 registers `T-CAT-013` for `publishProduct`, `unpublishProduct`, `archiveProduct` and `restoreProduct`, with a unit test of the agreement versions still accepted. `T-SHOP-007` now asserts the owner's shop is created in `post` mode, and `T-ARCH-036` that the demo shop `demo-pasal` is. Twenty-seven deliberate breaks each failed a test. Two failed only after the test set `first_published_at` or `published_at` a day back, because the test's transaction fixes `now()` ([06 note 72](06-api-design.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
95. **The seller product pages' tests (2026-11-26, R1-S part 2f-i).** §6.9 registers `T-UI-042` for the product list, the new product page and the editor, as `T-UI-041` did for the shipping page: no registered ID covered them (`T-CAT-008` to `T-CAT-010` are the operations'). The parts this work adds to existing IDs are in their rows: `T-UI-008` (the product states), `T-SEC-001` (case (a) for the editor), `T-SEC-030`, `T-SEC-031`, `T-SEC-036` and `T-SEC-043`. Of thirteen deliberate breaks, each failed a test: eight in the page controller and the form's choices (dropping the permission or the gate, the refused-parameter rule, the kept category or brand, the search, the leaf filter, the deepest-row rule) and five in the form's rules. After review: a bracketed key (`status[]=draft`) redirected to itself, now covered by two more refused-parameter rows. The browser half (the forms' focus and the 412 panel) was walked through by hand at 390 and 1280 px in both themes and waits for the browser suite.
96. **Fixture git commands and a worktree's hooks (2026-11-26).** Git exports `GIT_DIR` and the other variables of `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` to its hooks, and in a linked worktree `GIT_DIR` is an absolute path. The pre-push hook's unit run (09 §11.4) then made the fixture commands of the script tests (`tests/support/scripts.ts`, used by `T-SEC-025`, `T-ARCH-030` and the other repository checks) commit, branch and re-initialise the real repository instead of their temporary folders, and 16 tests of the unit suite failed in that run. The helpers now start every child without those variables (`isolatedEnv`). Checked by running the three git-using script specs with `GIT_DIR` pointing at a throwaway repository: with the old helper 15 of their 34 tests failed and the repository was changed; with the new one all passed and it was left untouched; the whole unit suite run the same way also passed and left it untouched. The main checkout was not affected, because its hooks see the relative `GIT_DIR=.git`.
97. **The bundle budget and the seller catalog (2026-11-26, R1-S part 2f-i).** `T-UI-012` failed the first push of 2f-i: every page carried every catalog, and the product pages' strings took `account/addresses` from 249.1 KB to 252.7 KB of JavaScript (gzip), over the 250 KB storefront budget. `seller.json` now loads with the seller pages ([09 note 132](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)), and `T-UI-034` gains its cases. Of two deliberate breaks (a `seller.*` key in the shared site header, a load that runs on every call), both failed a test. After review the scan also refuses a template literal that starts with `seller.` and walks `shared/` too. `scripts/check_bundle.mjs` follows static imports only, so the seller catalog's chunk (5.2 KB gzip) counts for no route, the seller pages included, though each waits for it before it renders ([08 note 91](08-ui-ux-and-design-system.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)). In a browser on the development server, `/account` fetched no seller catalog, a client visit to the seller overview fetched it once and showed its text, and a seller page opened directly showed no raw key.
98. **The storefront's reference reads and navigation entries (2026-11-26, R1-S part 3a).** §6.5 registers `T-CAT-015` for `listCategories` and `listAttributes`, and builds `T-CAT-107` against `app/modules/catalog/navigation.ts`. Eighteen deliberate breaks each failed a test ([06 note 73](06-api-design.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
99. **The dashboard layouts and the bundle check (2026-11-26).** With the seller and admin layouts loading with their surface ([09 note 134](09-code-structure-and-engineering-standards.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)), `scripts/check_bundle.mjs` counts, for each page, the chunks of its surface's layout (`inertia/layouts/<surface>_layout.tsx`) and catalog (`resources/lang/en/<surface>.json`) when they are dynamic, so note 97's uncounted seller catalog is now counted on the seller pages. Three rules join `T-UI-012`: a storefront route that loads a dashboard layout fails; a layout or catalog loaded on demand that no page counts fails, so one named otherwise cannot go uncounted; and a seller or admin layout that is not a chunk loaded on demand fails, because a static import would inline it into the entry and so into every page. Four new fixture cases in `tests/unit/scripts/check_bundle.spec.ts`, and the seller route case gains its layout. Of four deliberate breaks (not counting the surface's chunks, and dropping each of the three rules), each failed a test. Measured by the Static job of the pull request, against `926e511`, the first green Static job after the catalog moved out: `errors/not_found` 182.0 KB (197.7 KB before), `storefront/home` 181.3 KB, `account/addresses` 240.2 KB (245.9 KB), and `seller/products` 220.7 KB (209.8 KB), now with its layout and `seller.json` counted. Vite keys a manifest entry by its source path relative to the project root, so the catalog's key is `resources/lang/en/seller.json`, the name the check looks for.
100. **The browser suite's transaction, and `T-CAT-006` (2026-11-26).** §3.3 records that `tests/bootstrap.ts` wraps only the functional suite so far, and the four points the first browser spec must settle when it adds the wrap: closing the browser context before the rollback, parallel requests sharing one transaction, the memory session store of `sessionBrowserClient`, and committed limiter rows. A wrap added without them was reviewed and withdrawn. §6's `T-CAT-006` row adds a later listing page's canonical, the `per_page` and past-the-last-page rules, and the `X-Robots-Tag` header of `/checkout`, after [ADR-0017](adr/0017-product-urls-public-id.md) decision 8 was edited.
101. **The storefront listing's tests (2026-11-27, R1-S part 3b).** §6.5 registers `T-CAT-014` for `listProducts` and its query parser, and builds `T-CAT-003`. The listing rows are written directly, with exact prices, dates and value IDs, on factory products; `T-CAT-012` covers how `catalog.refresh_listing` builds them. Thirty-three deliberate breaks each failed a test; one needed a page holding exactly `per_page` cards ([06 note 74](06-api-design.md#consistency-notes-for-editor)).
